title: [Showcase] tt-ai-screener: An AI-powered Stock Screener & Analyzer (MCP Server integrated)
author: YoYo1675
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I wanted to share a project I've been working on: **tt-ai-screener** 

**GitHub Repository:** `giordanoshai/tt-ai-screener`

# Capabilities

* **Long-term Screening:** Find high-growth, high-margin stocks trading above their 200-day Moving Average.
* **Swing Trade Screening:** Detect breakout or pullback setups with volume confirmation.
* **Position Review:** Analyze technicals + fundamentals + news + P&L for your current holdings.
* **Watchlist Analysis:** Batch analyze all your tracked tickers in one go.

# Data Handled

* **Technical Indicators:** 2 years of daily OHLCV data, RSI, MA, and ATR.
* **Fundamentals:** P/E ratio, margins, growth metrics, analyst ratings, earnings, and insider transactions.
* **Market Context:** Last 30 days of news and news sentiment analysis.

# Features

* **MCP Server Support:** Seamlessly connect it to Claude.ai or any other LLM supporting the Model Context Protocol.
* **Custom Prompts:** You can customize your own prompt templates to guide the LLM's investment analysis style.

# What You Need to Run It

* **Finnhub API Key** (Free or Premium tier) for market and fundamental data.
* **At least 2 LLM API Keys** for running the news sentiment analysis and advanced screening skills.

comments.author: Either_Door_5500
comments.body:
Building an AI-powered screener with an MCP server is an awesome approach to solving context limits and data retrieval for LLMs. The hardest part with financial AI agents is always preventing hallucinations when they read raw text or messy financial tables.

For an effective AI screening workflow, feeding the model pre-structured, clean fundamental data directly extracted from regulatory filings makes a massive difference in response accuracy and processing speed.

Curious if you've seen data quality issues with your existing data providers? In my own experience, a lot of them actually have quite a few hidden in their data + aren't really transparent about the source.

Another pain point I've seen is pricing. The pricing cliffs for data are sometimes beyond reasonable for many, effectively pricing out a large set of developers right from the get-go.  

I've been working on an api in this space - High quality fundamentals, based on SEC data and with clean amendment trails linking back to actual filings. All priced fairly without compromising data quality. This might be useful for expanding your mcp server capabilities.

Happy to share more if you want to take a look.

replies.author: YoYo1675
replies.body:
Some data providers are indeed way too expensive for individual developers.   
 A lot of my data is currently sourced from free tiers like Yahoo Finance and Finnhub, which makes it hard for me to verify the absolute accuracy of the data. Personally, I think if there are any errors, they're most likely in the OHLCV data. However, a slight deviation there shouldn't have a huge impact on my AI stock screener workflow.
